caption:
We debated posting about this, but we know too many people loved Pitty to not share. Unfortunately, this last week, Pitty passed away. He had a viral infection that was silently attacking his organs and caused a blood clot on his bladder. Despite having seen a vet regularly, we knew none of this and saw no signs. The blood clot ruptured, and made his situation fatal in less than a day. 

We got Pitty right at 8 weeks old and immediately fell in love with him! He truly was a huge part of such an important chapter for our relationship. Pitty loved reggae music in the backyard, Frank Sinatra before his 2:30 pm nap, sour skittles, whip cream, crunchy food, dandelions, the warm fire place, belly scratches, his camo blanket, and all his friends and family. We are so grateful for the time we got with Mr. Pitty. We will love him forever and are happy knowing we got to share Pitty with so many of you!🤍

caption:
There are times you’re told you’re too emotional or too much, cry in your car after practice, play through pain, and learn how to take up space in rooms that weren’t built for you. Being a woman in sports has taught me resilience in ways nothing else ever could. How to fail loudly, fight quietly, love something so deeply you’re willing to do anything for it, and stand back up when life knocks you to the ground. Some days I feel powerful, some days I feel broken, but most days I feel so beyond grateful. Grateful for my strong teammates, grateful for little girls watching, grateful for every chance to chase a dream that once felt impossible. To every girl grinding when no one is watching, I see you. To every woman who fought for the space we occupy today, thank you. To my younger self who just wanted to belong somewhere, you made it. Here’s to strong women, soft hearts, scars, setbacks, and comebacks. 
Happy Girls and Women in Sports Day 🤍
#girlsandwomeninsportsday

To 2025 thank you for helping me grow into a better version of myself. You forced me to slow down, look within myself and find my “why.” Behind the smiles was a kid quietly battling depression, fighting through moments nobody ever saw but I never gave up. You sat me down to build my character, humbled my heart, and pulled me closer to God. Every setback became a lesson, every tear turned into strength, and every prayer reminded me I wasn’t alone.

I’m walking into 2026 with faith, peace, and purpose. This year, I’m choosing joy on purpose. I’m choosing discipline, alignment, healing, and growth. I’m ready for new challenges, new blessings, and everything God has prepared for me. No more doubting, no more shrinking just stepping into who I’m meant to be.

caption: Oh volleyball… I could never thank you enough for this crazy journey. I truly am so grateful for it all. God has given me all of these opportunities that not many people get to experience. I have met so many people along the way and some have become my very best friends. Closing this chapter of my life is going to be tough and honestly is going to be a weird adjustment, but I am so excited for what the future has to hold. We are SO much more than the sport that we play. Big thank you to everyone who has supported me throughout my whole career, I really could not thank you all enough. To every teammate and coach I’ve ever had, thank you for having such a big impact on my life. I have so much gratitude for the Arkansas, Elkhorn South, Nebraska Juniors, Nebraska Elite, and St. Patrick’s (where it all started) volleyball programs. To all of my family, thank you for sticking with me through the good and bad days. You all have been my “why” throughout the years. I love and appreciate you all so much. Nowww next up is grad school (location TBD) and my journey of becoming a Speech-Language Pathologist!!! 💖📚💬

caption: for almost 20 years, soccer has not just been something i’ve done, but a part of who i am. i’ve never known a version of myself that isn’t a soccer player, and honestly i don’t really want to, because all the very best parts of myself i owe to this sport. i’m not sure how you’re supposed to let go of something like that, but i do know that i will be forever thanking God for trusting me with such an incredible gift—one that filled me with so much joy, took me to so many amazing places, gave me so many incredible people, left me with so many memories, and through it all, has shown me His faithfulness again and again. even though it’s time to hang up the cleats, i know all the things soccer has given me, all the incredible ways it has shaped me, will be with me for the rest of my life, and i am a better person because of it. thank you soccer for both the most challenging and most beautiful last 18 years of my life. and thank you Jesus for giving me something that hurts this bad to say goodbye to.

caption:
I actually can’t believe I made it this far…

From Tulsa to OU to Arkansas was a physically, mentally, and spiritually painful journey. A journey nonetheless I would do all over again. All I can express is extreme gratitude for the losses and the wins because Lord knows the losses were incomparable with the gains. “For I consider that the sufferings of this present time are not worth comparing with the glory that is to be revealed to us. -Romans 8:18” these past few days have been nothing but genuine Love. Love that is gentle, love that is patient , and love that is kind. The love I have received has been long suffering, and is given with grace. Thank you to my family for always, and I mean ALWAYS supporting me, even when it didn’t make sense. Glory be to God for all that has happened, is happening, and is to come. With that being said..

caption:
🇨🇴 ORGULLO COLOMBIANO
María José Marín, la Caleña que representa a Colombia en lo más alto del golf mundial, es oficialmente campeona del WALA 2025. 🏆⛳️

Así es: la Caleña se coronó campeona del Women’s Amateur Latin America 2025, después de un desempate intensísimo a tres hoyos contra la barbadense Emily Odwin.
Pero Majo sacó su mejor versión, la versión de una campeona. 🏌️‍♀️

🔥 La estrella colombiana conquistó el PGA de Riviera Maya y reafirmó por qué es la mejor latinoamericana del ranking mundial amateur y la actual campeona individual de la NCAA.
Este es su primer título WALA, y lo hizo cerrando con una ronda impresionante de -8 golpes (68 en total). Brutal.

Y lo más inspirador: esto ya lo había visualizado. Te mostramos aquí un pequeño fragmento donde le decía a su ídolo, Annika, que soñaba con conocerla y jugar su competencia.
Hoy, no solo lo cumplió… sino que lo ganó. Frente a su ídolo.
Eso no lo hace cualquiera.

👏 Felicitaciones, Majo.
No es lo mismo cumplir un sueño, que cumplirlo siendo campeona… y siendo campeona frente a quien más admiras.

Comenta si también estás orgulloso de lo que logró Majo. 🇨🇴💛💙❤️
#GolfColombia #WALA2025 #MariaJoseMarin #OrgulloColombiano #GolfLatam GolfLife Briceño18

caption:
NCAA 2025!! 🏆

It’s not the ending we hoped for, but I am incredibly grateful for every moment of this week. ELITE 8 and I achieved the last goal I had left…. becoming an All-American🇺🇸 for the first time in 16 years.
I would like to thank my coaches @tuckerclary13 @richard_sipala for believing in me, for their patience, for giving me what I needed at every moment, coconut water, coffee with PPC, holding the umbrella, coke :)... and for pushing me when I needed it most. Also to @koskel and the best teammates in the world @razorbackwten, without them I wouldn’t be the player or person I am today, and every moment this fall has been incredible. Of course, thanks to my family who always support me from home and to that person who has always pushed me to believe in myself and know that I can win. Finally, thank you very much to @razorbackwten @arkrazorbacks @uarkansas and everyone who texted me and supported me this week and this fall. Forever thankful!! See you in the spring🐗❤️

#arkansas #ncaatournament #elite8 #razorbacks #pinkponyclub

athlete.bio: A relentless competitor with a penchant for precision, this athlete combines agility and intellect on the field. Off the turf, his infectious enthusiasm and unwavering determination inspire teammates and fans alike.

caption:
It still doesn’t feel real. I can’t stop thinking about you. Every time I close my eyes, the memories hit me, and I break down all over again. I’ve cried more in these last two days than I ever have in my life.😭💔

You weren’t just a brother to me — you were someone I looked up to, someone who pushed me, protected me, and believed in me even when I didn’t believe in myself. I keep wishing I could hear your voice one more time or tell you all the things I didn’t get to say.

It hurts so much knowing you’re not here, but I promise you this: I’m going to make you proud. Everything I do from here on out, I’m carrying your name, your strength, and your spirit with me. I’m not stopping and not giving up because you always believed in me. 

Thank you for every moment, every lesson, every laugh. I love you forever, big bro. Rest easy 🙏🏼

caption:
Most runners chase medals. Yaseen Abdalla chases the line between life and collapse.

Yaseen Abdalla’s story is a masterclass in grit, faith, and the war between ambition and balance.

From anchoring Texas to an NCAA title → representing Sudan at the Olympics → placing 21st at Worlds after nearly destroying his body — this episode is not just about running. It’s about how far you’re willing to go to find out what you’re made of.

He breaks down:

💀 What it feels like to push your body past its limits (yes, blood involved)

⚡️ Why most runners never reach their potential — and how to outwork “lack of talent”

🧠 The truth about lazy athletes, bad coaches, and why you should be “failure maxing”

💥 Why balance — not grind — is the language of the universe

This is raw truth from one of the most honest voices in the sport.

If you’ve ever questioned how badly you want it — listen to this.

caption:
Malé zastavení mi připomnělo velké dary.

Upřímně řečeno, toto nutné zpomalení mi ze začátku přinášelo lehkou úzkost. Jsem zvyklá být stále v pohybu, pracovat, učit se, mít rutinu a rozvíjet se každý den. Přesto mi tato chvíle umožnila uvědomit si, co je opravdu podstatné.
Dala mi prostor ocenit lidi kolem sebe, své tělo jako dar od Boha a všechny možnosti, které mám - chodit do školy, plavat, být součástí kolektivu, který mě podporuje a pomáhá mi růst. Tento čas mi připomněl, jak důležitá je vděčnost.
Bylo a stále je pro mě těžké přijmout, že zotavení je pomalý proces a že mozek si opravdu žádá čas. Přesto mi ukázal, že i když zpomalíme, můžeme růst a že naše hodnota není určena rychlostí, výsledky ani výkonem, ale tím, kým jsme a jak věříme.

caption:
Elmir Džafić je prošao jednogodišnji individualni program u KK Bosna kroz koji je značajno napredovao u ključnim detaljima važnim za njegovu karijeru.

Glavni akcenat bio je na šutu, koji je ranije bio biomehanički nepravilno izveden. Kroz specijalne vježbe korigovan je položaj ruke, tajming izbačaja i ulazak nogama u šut, što je postepeno donijelo stabilniju i pravilniju tehniku. Napredak se najviše vidio na treninzima, dok mu je na utakmicama u početku falila konstantnost, ali je kasnije automatizovao pokrete i dobio pravilan i biomehanički ispravan šut. 

Veliki iskorak napravio je i gubitkom 15kg mišićne mase tokom boravka u Americi, čime je postao brži i pokretljiviji, samim tim i sposoban da parira bekovima NCAA lige.

Danas Džafa ima dobar i pravilan šut i centarsku tehniku, što mu otvara velike mogućnosti u karijeri. Posebno me raduje njegov odlazak na koledž u Arkansasu, gdje će moći dalje da napreduje i potvrdi svoj potencijal. Džafa je perspektiva naše bosanskohercegovačke seniorske košarke. Jedva čekamo da gledamo njegove igre Arkanzasu i sve dalje pomake u njegovoj svijetloj karijeri. 🏀💪🏼

caption:
I SPY PINK!! 

Today is October 1st which marks the start of breast cancer awareness month. This month holds a special place in my heart and will forever. My rock, my best friend, my idol, and most of all my mom is a breast cancer SURVIVOR. Over the past few days while speaking at events, I’ve been reminded just how lucky I am to still be able to laugh, spend time, and make memories with my mom because many can’t say the same. A lot of people would have let the ever dreaded C word steal their light but instead my mom has let it be her fuel. She has made it her mission to spread awareness and support the foundation that helped save her life, the breast cancer research foundation. Every 1 and 8 women are diagnosed with breast cancer in their lifetime. Cancer affects more than just the one diagnosed, it steals moms from children, wives from husbands, friends from friends, siblings from siblings, and so much more. Take time to be grateful for your bodies and health. Help us change the world!  https://give.bcrf.org/fundraiser/5718582  The link will also be in my bio!

caption:
Pottery Gold 🤜💥🤛 Podium Gold

The Japanese art of Kintsugi holds a message: It’s our fractures reassembled that make us powerful and strong. And as every athlete knows, you can’t perform your best before first breaking your body down.

Those who practice Kintsugi well do so with obsession. And obsession is something @on elite track & field superstar Bella Whittaker (@b_whit215) knows a few things about.

I wanted to know more, so the two of us sat down in Tokyo to break down over broken pottery what obsession means in the pursuit of her dreams.

Two days later, Bella achieved one of those dreams, winning gold in the 4x4 relay on the world championships stage.

Congratulations Bella!! 👏🥇 🇯🇵

@on @b_whit215 #DreamOn

We are thrilled to announce a full-circle moment for The St. James Performance Academy and MVP League — welcome Aaliyah Pyatt as our newest Assistant Coach! 🎉

Aaliyah’s journey from elite athlete to mentor embodies exactly what we stand for: excellence, dedication, and legacy. As the last true High School National Champion in the 400m and a key member of the Arkansas Razorbacks, she helped secure 4 National Titles and 4 SEC Championships during her storied collegiate career.

Now, she brings that championship mindset, technical expertise, and profound love for the sport back to where it all began — to inspire the next generation of champions.

Join us in giving a huge welcome to “Coach Liyah” 🙌 Drop a 🔥 in the comments if you’re ready to learn from one of the best.

so much to be grateful for.
so much to carry with me. 🤍

this past week and a half was full of emotions my mind is still running.

you think waking at 6 a.m. (race day) makes you early, until you see the Chinese national team already running and stretching behind the hotel. 
you meet Koreans who greet you with kindness and warmth.
you watch Japanese swimmers bow to their team with quiet respect.
you hear the Americans lifting each other in the finals with pure team energy.

and of course - the fun at the end… who else but the Slovaks! 

Berlin was wild. ❤️‍🔥
and I’m deeply thankful I got to experience it.
proud to have stood on the starting blocks for my country.

caption:
World University Games 2025 

my heart is full - there’s so much i need to think through and pray about.
this competition has opened my eyes in many ways.
my times weren’t quite where i had hoped, but maybe that’s exactly what needed to happen.
this experience reminded me to pause, reflect, and be honest with myself about what i truly desire - and to give my whole heart to whatever comes next. 
all glory to God.
his timing is never rushed and never late.
even when i didn’t understand, He was teaching me patience and shaping me in the quiet.
i’m so thankful for His grace — without it, i wouldn’t be here. 
i’m deeply grateful to my family, who showed up and surprised me - your love gave me strength when i needed it most. 
to my teammates in Arkansas and Ostrava - thank you for showing up every day, pushing alongside me, and helping me grow, in and out of the water. 
to my coaches Alec, Neil, Paige, Lola and Libor and my strength coaches, Coach G and James - thank you for your patience, belief, and wisdom.
to my psychologist - thank you for helping me stay centered when things felt overwhelming. 
to Lauren and Emily - thank you for helping me through some tough moments with nutrition, and for never making me feel like I was failing. 
to Laura and Morgan - your care and support kept my body going, even when it was tired. i truly appreciate you. 
to Megan.

caption:
Paityn Noe has gone from being an injury-plagued freshman to one of the NCAA’s most electrifying distance runners, redefining success with speed, resilience, and purpose.

After a turbulent freshman year marked by injury and setbacks, Paityn didn’t just bounce back, she transformed, clocking a blazing 31:36.91 to break Arkansas’ 10,000m record, becoming All-American in the 10,000m and 5,000m outdoors, and finishing 4th at NCAA Outdoors.

Her resume reads like a breakout-year checklist: she ran 15:11.27 in the 5000m; 8:47.17 in the 3000m; she finished in 7th place at NCAA Cross Country Nationals; and she earned All-American honors in the 3,000m and 5,000m indoors.

But behind the accolades is a story of mindset, discipline, and a radically honest approach to fueling and recovery. 

Paityn has been candid about how embracing nourishment, faith, and joy became the foundation for her breakthrough. Now, she’s on a mission to change how young athletes think about performance.

Paityn’s discussion is equal parts blueprint and inspiration; an inside look at what it takes to turn adversity into acceleration.

In today’s conversation, Paityn walks me through her record breaking outdoor track season, bouncing back after a hard freshman year, placing 7th at the NCAA XC Championship meet, her goals and ambitions for this upcoming season, her thoughts on Breaking4, being raised in a coffee/ice cream shop, and so much more. 

Tap into the Paityn Noe Special.

athlete.bio: A relentless competitor with a penchant for precision, this athlete combines agility and intellect on the field. Off the turf, his infectious enthusiasm and unwavering determination inspire teammates and fans alike.

caption:
After 6 unforgettable years, my NCAA journey has officially come to an end. If you told that little boy from Taos, NM that he’d grow up to be a 7x All-American he probably would’ve just smiled. Because deep down, he always believed. From Adams State to Arkansas, track gave me more than medals or titles. It gave me purpose. It gave me a family. It gave me a place to grow, to fail, to rise, and to find out who I really am. There were days I doubted myself, days my body wanted to quit, and days I questioned the path. But somehow, with faith, love, and support, I kept going. 

Thank you to @adamsstatexctf @razorbacktfxc and everyone who believed in me, pushed me, cheered for me, and ran this race with me. Your support carried me through the highs and lows, and I’m forever grateful for every coach, teammate, friend, and family member who stood by me along the way.

This journey wasn’t just mine — it was ours.

Jonah signing off🫶🏼

athlete.bio: Hailing from a small town, this fierce competitor blends agility with a strategic mindset. Known for her infectious enthusiasm and unwavering determination, she inspires teammates while dazzling fans with her skillful play.

caption:
It’s hard to put into words what these last 4 years have meant to me. Track and field wasn’t just a sport it was a part of my identity, my therapy, my challenge, and my joy all wrapped into one. From the first practice to the final meet, I gave it everything I had… and somehow, it still gave me even more in return. What stays with me are the memories, the bus rides, the pre-meet nerves, the late night laughs, and the friendships that turned into family. I’ve grown not just as an athlete, but as a person. I’ve failed, I’ve succeeded, and I’ve learned what it truly means to keep going no matter what. I’ll miss the nervousness, the anxiety, the race jitters, the fear, excitement, and even the pre race shits😭.

Walking away from this chapter is heartbreaking, but it’s also beautiful. Because I know I’m leaving with a full heart. I found people who pushed me, inspired me, and stood by me through it all. Lifelong friends. Teammates I’ll never forget. Moments I’ll carry with me forever. I can’t say until next time cause this time there isn’t one.🫶🏽💔

Thank you, track and field. You’ll always have a piece of my heart.

caption:
THE OG BIG BANG THEORY. 💥

Every great program has that one athlete who shifts everything. For us that was Aaliyah Pyatt.

She took what others started and ignited something unstoppable. Our first true national champion. The last undisputed queen of the 400m before the sport split into three titles/meets. A trailblazer whose standard still shapes everything we do.

caption:
Oh to be an Arkansas Razorback 

If you would have told me 4 years ago that I would have been a collegiate athlete at one of the best if not best track schools in the world, i wouldn’t have believed you. This sport has been a roller coaster of ups and downs but I am forever grateful for the friendships, memories, life lessons, and growth that I have gained from it. The last season was one that won’t be forgotten, 3 indoor PRs and 2 outdoor PRs which led to dropping 5 seconds overall in the 800. Though I am sad to let this part of my life go, it’s not the end of my story just a chapter in my book of life. Thank you Arkansas T&F for leading me to my best friend and preparing to take on any feat that comes my way. Thank you Taylor Washington for taking me under your wing when I needed it most and Coach Johnson for making sure to give me a hard time that always ended up in a laugh. Lastly, thank you for my support system that I couldn’t have done it without. I can’t wait to see what my future holds! ❤️🐗#woopig #sub2:10club

caption:
College Days Swiftly Pass 🎓

I’m proud to announce that I will be graduating from the University of Arkansas with a Bachelor’s degree in Sports Management on May 10th at 12:30 PM!

It has been a long time coming, but the work is far from done. I thank God for giving me the strength, endurance, and countless blessings along the way. “I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me.” — Philippians 4:13.

I want to sincerely thank my parents, family members, friends, brothers, and teammates for all the love and support throughout this journey.

Thank you to @razorbacktfxc and the coaching staff for believing in me as a young freshman and developing me into a multi-time All-American. It has truly been a blessing. I also want to thank the brothers of the Kappa Kappa Chapter of Alpha Phi Alpha Fraternity, Inc., and my line brothers — the 8.P.E.S — for the brotherhood, love, and influence you have had on my life. College days swiftly pass, imbued with mem’ries fond.

Master’s up next…

caption:
Year 3!!! Not the one I expected, after many months of wrist pain and treatments, I decided to have surgery and take some time off, everything went well and I am ready to start the recovery. Thank you so much to Dr Brannan and his medical team for helping me and giving me the best care. Many thanks also to the UARK medical team for helping and advising me at all times. 

It has not been the best tennis year but I am very grateful to my team, teammates and coaches for supporting me when I was in bad times and in good times too. Thanks to them I have achieved for the third consecutive year to be named All SEC second team! 🏆🐗❤️

Finally thank you so much to my family, my parents, my sister and my boyfriend, without you nothing would have been possible and this way would be different. 
I can’t wait to show what comes next but I’m very excited! 🔜

Thank you Razorback family for the support that I receive every day, i look forward to returning for my senior year!! @razorbackwten 

Carolina👸🏽

GOD’s Timing is designed to teach you to TRUST 

I still get frustrated sometimes, and have a long way to go…but it’s good to look back and remind myself of how far I’ve come🙌🏾
_______

Some Context…

During the last 3 weeks of November 2024, I began experiencing pain at the top of my right foot. At the beginning of December 2024, I could not walk without limping and needed a boot. After taking an MRI & CT scan, my doctor confirmed that I had a grade 2 fracture of the navicular bone, months in the making (the bone was split halfway through).

I had surgery the next week which involved obtaining bone marrow from my pelvis to inject into the fracture site, and the addition of a titanium screw making me bionic :) [Yes it will remain in my foot]
This was followed by weeks of no weight bearing, lots of hopping, the help of others, and the use of crutches or a knee scooter to move around, along with rehab, rehab, and more rehab😃

But I’m slowly and surely getting stronger and better.

caption:
Ooh, I’ve been procrastinating on posting this, but here it goes!

It’s been an incredible rollercoaster 4 1/2 years in college and I’m beyond grateful for the journey. A huge thank you to @bartoncc_xctf for taking a chance on me, for seeing my potential from the very beginning. Those two years were truly special—being in a place of nowhere and turning it into somewhere. To all the coaches and mentors who guided me, kept me on track, and pushed me to be better—thank you! The foundation you helped build has carried me through, and I’ll always appreciate the impact you’ve had on my life. 

Then came the next chapter at USF, where I faced many obstacles, both on and off the track. It was a challenging period, but one that ultimately led to a turning point in my life. Through it all, I found a way to regain my strength and refocus on the sport I love so much. A huge thank you to @usfxctf for the growth “ that came from on and off the track” lessons, the struggles. That chapter shaped me in ways I never expected, and for that, I’m very grateful.

Finally, the last chapter of my collegiate journey led me to the @razorbacktfxc where I earned my bachelor’s degree, a dream I’ve always had. Being part of a winning legacy was something I aspired to, and I’m beyond grateful not only to have been a part of it but to have contributed to those SEC and national titles. I’m walking away with strength, confidence, and power, knowing that every challenge along the way shaped me into the person I am today! 
 
To my athletic staff, supports, families, and friends thank you so much I love yall❤️ thanks for making this journey nothing short of amazing. Nia Robinson Signout>>>

caption:
and the leg lived to see another day
4 surgeries, 70 stitches, 2 broken bones, a metal rod and 4 screws, PICC line, infection, compartment syndrome and almost a month in the hospital later…
to the girl who didn’t know if she would have a leg or was told she may never walk normal again, we made it!! from learning how to do the daily life skills again and relearn how to use my leg completely came with the darkest times. it was my people that kept me together allowing me to overcome this and i couldn’t more grateful. to my family who dropped everything to be there and to my best friends and teammates who never left my side once. they continued to surround me with love and put a smile on my face when that was the last thing I wanted. they gave me faith and gave me the power to know i would see the light at this end of this tunnel when it felt like the world was crashing down. to the coaches and doctors, nurses, PTs, and ATs who never lost hope and were there every step of the way… I thank yall forever and ever and love yall more than i could ever put in words. 
And to the little girls dream it was to play soccer and who never would have thought I would ever walk again we are running again and soccer is coming so soon!! 
and to any girl struggling right now going through something like this i hope sharing my story will help you : God is good and you are strong enough to push past ❤️

athlete.name: Cale Kassen
athlete.bio: A tenacious competitor from the heart of Arkansas, this player blends agility with strategic finesse. Known for relentless hustle and a spirited attitude, he thrives under pressure, inspiring teammates with every play.

caption:
As I sit down to reflect on the journey I've embarked upon since 2021, it's hard not to feel a profound sense of gratitude and disbelief. It was a time when the words "you will never run again" echoed in my ears, and the possibility of amputating my leg loomed over me like a dark cloud. The thought of losing my leg and with it, my dreams in track and field, was almost too much to bear. But here I am, not just running, but excelling, having been named a 6-time All-American and setting a D2 record in my second-ever heptathlon. This transformation is nothing short of a miracle, and it's a testament to the power of perseverance, the right support, and an unwavering belief in oneself. 
▶️I cannot overstate the role @lanefletch11 has played in this remarkable journey. When hope was dimming, and the love for track and field was fading, Coach Feltcher reignited the flame. With unwavering support, belief in my potential, and a coaching approach that was both innovative and empathetic, he helped me find my way back to not just competing but thriving in the sport I love. The impact of such mentorship goes beyond medals and records; it's about rediscovering one's passion and proving that with the right support, anythings possible. ▶️Equally pivotal  in this journey was @leetfxccoach who took a chance on an injured athlete when others might’ve hesitated. That leap of faith was the catalyst from my comeback. It’s not just about the physical rehabilitation, but the psychological boost that comes from being believed in. His support was instrumental and rebuilding, not just my leg, but my confidence and determination over all the odds. ▶️With the heart full of gratitude for the coaches, teammates, family, and friends who have support me through this incredible journey, I am thrilled to announce my commitment to the university of Arkansas this decision marks a new chapter and my track and field career one that I approach with excitement, humility, and a deep sense of purpose. Call Dem Pigs! Wooo Pigs. 🐗🐗

caption:
little me would be so proud that i can finally fulfill my dreams and goals of being a d1 gymnast. i am so excited to announce my commitment to the university of arkansas on a full-ride athletic scholarship. the second i had my call on june 15 with jordyn i felt an instant connection. her goals for the program and how driven the staff is amazed me. the program they are building is what i knew i wanted to be apart of. 

thank you so much to my mom dad and sister for everything they have done for me. picking up and moving away from our friends and family 2 days before school started was not easy. i thank you for every single thing you have done and gave up for me in order to reach my goal. thank you tct gymnastics. without tct i would not be where i am today and i am extremely grateful for the unconditional love and support i get from the team and the coaches. you never gave up on me even when i wanted to give up on myself.  i want to say thank you to AJ and danielle. thank you for starting me off on my journey of become a gymnast and making me have a goal to be a d1 gymnast. you guys always cared about me as a person over me as a gymnast. you never made me feel less than what i was worth. thank you for the last 10 years to the beginning of my journey. i have been so fortunate to have met so many amazing coaches and learned about their great programs throughout this process. 

lookout SEC, the HOGS are coming! #committed

To my big brother, #1 fan, best friend, JJ

  I am so proud of you, j-rich. You were the most humble, giving, and loving person I knew. Losing you has left a hole in our family and community that will never be filled. I will never ever forget all the memories we shared together. You were always there for me, from cheering me on at any of my sports events to picking me up if I had a bad day, and I will forever be so so grateful for that. You were taken from us too soon, J, but I am so thankful for the 17 years I got to love you. I will forever carry your memory and love in my heart, and I will never forget your HUGE smile and contagious laugh. I will try to live the rest of my life as you lived yours, loving and helping everyone in any way I can, focusing on the important things. You were the best role model to look up to, and you showed me what a true man is. Reagan and I are physically 2/3 now, but we are forever 3/3. You complete us

Rest in peace, j-swole.
